title: Reject incompatible flows before constructing injection events
answers: Why does injecting a WebSocket message into @focus crash?
How should message injection handle a flow of the wrong protocol?
What flow checks must WebSocket, TCP, and UDP injection preserve?
body:
Symptom: Injecting messages into an incompatible flow or passing a bare @focus string can crash with AttributeError instead of only logging a warning.
Root cause: mitmproxy/addons/proxyserver.py:Proxyserver.inject_websocket, Proxyserver.inject_tcp, and Proxyserver.inject_udp logged failed flow checks but continued constructing events and calling inject_event, which accesses flow.client_conn.
Fix pattern: Return immediately after the incompatible-flow warning, before constructing messages or injection events.
Constraints: WebSocket injection requires an HTTPFlow with websocket present; TCP and UDP injection require their respective flow types. Passing these checks does not establish a live connection: correctly typed flows must still reach the existing live-connection check.
applies: Changes to WebSocket, TCP, or UDP message injection in Proxyserver.
